title: After Hours Care
description: Know where to seek help when we are closed, from after-hours GP care to emergency services.
headings: Mater Hospital Brisbane Adult Emergency Department
text: Patient Information After Hours Care Know where to seek help when we are closed, from after-hours GP care to emergency services. Information for patients of Woolloongabba Medical Centre in Brisbane’s inner south. Need medical help now? Choose the safest next step. Call Clinic Hello Home Doctor — 134 100 13 HEALTH Emergency — Call 000 Choose the right next step Use the option that best matches what is happening now. Clinic open — Call reception Life-threatening emergency — Call 000 Clinic closed — Call Hello Home Doctor Unsure what care you need — Call 13 HEALTH When we are open During normal opening hours, contact reception on (07) 3217 3344 for appointment availability and advice about the most appropriate next step. For life-threatening illness or injury, call Triple Zero (000) rather than waiting for a routine appointment. For a life-threatening illness or injury Call Triple Zero (000) and ask for an ambulance. Queensland Health advises emergency care for symptoms such as severe breathing difficulty, chest pain, severe bleeding, major trauma or other life-threatening conditions. Call 000 Hello Home Doctor When the practice is closed, patients can contact Hello Home Doctor on 134 100 or use its online booking service. Hello Home Doctor is an accredited after-hours medical deputising service providing GP home visits and, where clinically appropriate, telehealth. Published consultation hours: Monday to Friday 6:00 PM–8:00 AM; Saturday from midday; Sunday and public holidays 24 hours. Its call centre is open 24 hours to receive and triage requests. Eligibility, service coverage, attendance times and bulk-billing conditions can vary. Hello Home Doctor advises patients to call 134 100 to confirm coverage and eligibility. This service is not for emergencies. Visit Hello Home Doctor → 13 HEALTH If you are unsure what level of care you need, Queenslanders can call 13 HEALTH — 13 43 25 84 . Registered nurses provide health assessment and advice 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. Queensland Health care options Nearby emergency departments Princess Alexandra Hospital 199 Ipswich Road, Woolloongabba QLD 4102 · Emergency services operate 24 hours. Mater Hospital Brisbane Adult Emergency Department Raymond Terrace, South Brisbane QLD 4101 · 24-hour adult emergency service · 07 3163 8111. In an emergency, do not delay care while comparing hospitals or waiting times — call 000. After-hours questions What should I do in a life-threatening emergency? Call Triple Zero (000) and ask for an ambulance. Do not wait for a routine appointment when symptoms are life-threatening. What after-hours service can I use when Woolloongabba Medical Centre is closed? When we are closed, contact Hello Home Doctor on 134 100 or use its online booking service. It provides after-hours GP home visits and, where clinically appropriate, telehealth. Eligibility and coverage conditions apply. What if I am unsure which after-hours option is appropriate? If you are unsure what level of care you need, Queenslanders can call 13 HEALTH on 13 43 25 84 for health assessment and advice from registered nurses, 24 hours a day, 7 days a week. title: HotDoc Message Safety
h1: Identifying scam messages from authentic messages we send via HotDoc
description: How to recognise genuine HotDoc appointment, recall, correspondence and consent messages from Woolloongabba Medical Centre — and what to do if unsure.
headings: Why you may receive messages from us
We use HotDoc to reach you securely.
text: Patient Information Identifying scam messages from authentic messages we send via HotDoc Woolloongabba Medical Centre uses HotDoc as an approved platform for patient communications. This page helps you recognise legitimate messages and respond safely if something looks suspicious. Explore related pages Unsure about a message? Call the clinic before you click, reply or share personal details. Book Appointment Call Clinic Why you may receive messages from us We may contact you about appointments, reminders, recalls for results or follow-up, specialist or other correspondence that needs your attention, and Medicare bulk billing consent (Assignment of Benefit) requests. Messages can arrive as SMS, email or HotDoc app notifications, depending on the situation and your contact preferences. Approved platform We use HotDoc to reach you securely. Woolloongabba Medical Centre uses HotDoc as an approved patient communication partner. A HotDoc message may ask you to verify your identity before you view a health message or complete a consent request. That verification is usually limited to details such as your last name and date of birth. Examples of legitimate messages Appointment reminders — prompts to confirm, change or cancel an upcoming appointment, including HotDoc app push notifications. Recall messages — requests to book follow-up after test results, correspondence or recommended care. Correspondence notifications — alerts that a letter or report needs review with your doctor. Consent requests — short SMS or email links so Medicare bulk billing consent can be completed when required. Legitimate HotDoc emails typically come from hotdoc.com.au or hotdocmail.com.au . Legitimate links usually open hotdoc.com.au or short links on htd.io . Content often includes your name, our practice name and appointment or care details already known to the clinic. Warning signs of suspicious messages Requests for passwords, banking details, credit card numbers or one-time banking codes. Urgent threats, prizes, or pressure to act immediately without a clear clinical reason. Links that do not go to hotdoc.com.au or htd.io, or email addresses that only look similar to HotDoc. Poor spelling, unexpected attachments, or messages that do not mention Woolloongabba Medical Centre or your known care. If you are unsure Call the clinic on (07) 3217 3344 before responding. Never provide passwords or banking details in reply to a message claiming to be from us or HotDoc. HotDoc message questions Does Woolloongabba Medical Centre use HotDoc? Yes. We use HotDoc as an approved communication and booking platform for appointment reminders, recalls, correspondence notifications, consent requests and online booking. Booking & HotDoc → What do legitimate HotDoc messages look like? Legitimate messages usually name our practice, relate to your care, and use HotDoc domains such as hotdoc.com.au, hotdocmail.com.au or short links on htd.io. They may ask you to verify your last name and date of birth before viewing a health message. They never ask for passwords or banking details. What should I do if I am unsure about a message? Do not click the link or reply with personal or financial details. Call Woolloongabba Medical Centre on (07) 3217 3344 and ask reception to confirm whether a message was sent. Contact the clinic → Will you ever ask for my banking password? No. We will never ask for passwords, banking logins, or one-time codes for bank accounts by SMS, email or HotDoc. Treat any such request as suspicious. Related information Booking & HotDoc → Recalls & Reminders → Contact → This page provides general patient information about practice communications. It is not legal, financial or cybersecurity advice. If you believe you have shared sensitive details with a suspicious message, contact your bank or relevant provider and call the clinic if the message appeared to relate to your care.

title: Recalls and Reminders
description: How Woolloongabba Medical Centre uses recalls and reminders for results, correspondence, follow-up and preventive care — including HotDoc messages.
headings: Recall or reminder — what is the difference?
When patients may receive a recall
How HotDoc may deliver these messages
Keep your contact details up to date
text: Patient Information Recalls and reminders When follow-up is needed, we may recall you for review or send a reminder about upcoming care. Keeping your contact details current helps us reach you. Explore related pages Received a recall? Book the recommended follow-up, or call reception if you are unsure what is needed. Book Appointment Call Clinic Recall or reminder — what is the difference? Reminders help you keep an existing appointment or preventive task on track — for example confirming or cancelling a booking. Recalls ask you to return or book because follow-up is needed for your care. Both support continuity; a recall is more likely when something in your record needs review. When patients may receive a recall Test results — when a result should be discussed with a doctor or follow-up is advised. Specialist correspondence — when a letter or report needs review and a next step. Follow-up care — when your doctor has recommended review after treatment, procedures or ongoing concerns. Preventive care reminders — when screening, immunisation or other preventive care is due for discussion. Not every result or letter leads to a call. If your doctor asked you to return, please book even if you have not been contacted. How HotDoc may deliver these messages Woolloongabba Medical Centre may use HotDoc to send appointment reminders and health messages. Depending on your settings, you may receive an SMS, email or app notification. Some messages ask you to verify your identity before viewing details or booking. For help recognising legitimate HotDoc messages, see Identifying HotDoc scam messages . Keep your contact details up to date Please keep your mobile number, email and address current so the team can reach you when follow-up is required. Tell reception when details change, or update them when you complete patient forms. Your responsibility If you were asked to return for results or follow-up, make the appointment even if we have not contacted you. Recall and reminder questions What is the difference between a recall and a reminder? A reminder usually supports an appointment or preventive task you already know about, such as confirming an upcoming visit. A recall asks you to return or book because follow-up is clinically appropriate — for example after results, correspondence or recommended care. When might I receive a recall? You may receive a recall after test results, specialist or other correspondence, follow-up care recommended by your doctor, or preventive care that is due. The exact reason depends on your clinical record. Test results → Will recalls come through HotDoc? Yes, HotDoc may be used to deliver recall and reminder messages by SMS, email or app notification. You can also contact the clinic directly if you prefer to book by phone. Book Appointment Why do you need my current contact details? Accurate phone, email and address details help the team reach you when follow-up is required. Update your details with reception or when completing patient forms. New patients → Related information Contact → New Patients → Book Appointment → This page provides general information about practice recall and reminder processes. It does not replace individual medical advice. If you are worried about symptoms or a result, book review or call the clinic.

title: Telehealth Information
description: Telehealth consultations may be available for eligible patients at Woolloongabba Medical Centre. Learn suitability, booking, Medicare rules and when in-person care is needed.
text: Patient Information Telehealth Telehealth consultations may be available for eligible patients when a face-to-face visit is not required, subject to clinical suitability, GP discretion and Medicare rules. Explore related pages Need a telehealth appointment? Book through HotDoc where a telehealth option is offered, or call reception for guidance. Book Appointment Call Clinic When telehealth may be suitable Telehealth consultations may be available for eligible patients when remote care is clinically appropriate. Appointment availability may vary by practitioner, appointment type and current practice arrangements. Telehealth is often used by existing patients. Depending on the clinical context, it may support: Follow-up consultations Discussion of results and next steps Medication reviews where clinically appropriate Healthcare planning when a physical examination is not required GP discretion applies. A practitioner may recommend an in-person consultation if examination, testing or treatment cannot be provided safely by phone or video. Clinical suitability first Convenience does not replace clinical judgement. If your doctor needs to examine you, you may be asked to attend the medical centre. Appointments Booking telehealth Where a telehealth appointment is offered, book through the available HotDoc appointment options or call reception on (07) 3217 3344 if you are unsure which appointment type is suitable. Book Appointment Call (07) 3217 3344 For booking help and HotDoc guidance, see Booking & HotDoc . Medicare eligibility For general practice telehealth, Medicare eligibility can depend on your relationship with our practice. Current Medicare rules allow GP telehealth items when, for example, you are registered in MyMedicare with our practice or you have had an eligible face-to-face Medicare service with us within the previous 12 months. Other rules and exemptions can apply. If you are unsure whether your telehealth consultation will be Medicare eligible, ask reception before the appointment. See also Medicare and Bulk Billing . Preparing for the appointment Keep your phone nearby and make sure we have your correct contact number. Choose a private place where you can speak comfortably. For video appointments, use a device with a working camera, microphone and reliable internet connection. Have your medication list or relevant information available if the consultation relates to ongoing care. Prescriptions after telehealth Where clinically appropriate, an electronic prescription may be issued as an SMS or email token that you can present to a participating pharmacy. Prescribing remains a clinical decision and may not be suitable for every medicine or every patient. For repeat prescription requests outside a consultation, see Repeat Scripts and our New Patient Prescribing guidance where relevant. Telehealth fees Where a telehealth consultation is privately billed, our current fee schedule lists a weekday telehealth consultation at $65 with a Medicare rebate of $42.85, and a weekend telehealth consultation at $80 with a Medicare rebate of $42.85. Video telehealth items are also listed on the current fee schedule. Medicare eligibility and the final billing arrangement depend on the appointment and current Medicare rules. Reception can confirm this before your consultation. Related fee information is also on Fees & Billing . Patient questions Telehealth questions Are telehealth consultations available? Telehealth consultations may be available for eligible patients when clinically suitable. Appointment availability can vary by practitioner, appointment type and current practice arrangements. Booking & HotDoc → When can telehealth be useful? Telehealth may be suitable for selected follow-up care, results discussions, medication reviews where clinically appropriate, and healthcare planning when a physical examination is not required. GP discretion applies. Telehealth service overview → Who is telehealth usually for? Telehealth is often used by existing patients for suitable follow-up care. Medicare eligibility can depend on your relationship with the practice. Ask reception if you are unsure. New patients → What happens if my doctor needs to examine me? If the concern cannot be safely assessed remotely, you may be asked to attend the medical centre or another appropriate in-person service. Book Appointment Can prescriptions be issued after telehealth? Prescribing depends on the medication, your history and the doctor’s assessment. Some medicines require further review or an in-person consultation. Repeat prescriptions → More telehealth FAQs → Related information Telehealth service overview → Booking & HotDoc → Medicare → Test Results → Book Appointment → This page provides general patient information about telehealth at Woolloongabba Medical Centre. It does not replace individual medical advice. Telehealth is not an emergency service. For a life-threatening emergency, call Triple Zero (000).
